correctness.rationale: For admissible sets omitting the hub, two-step predecessor closure forces the odd parity stable set in even order and makes nonempty examples impossible in odd order. For complete sets containing the hub, conflict-freeness and completeness uniquely force the reset/alternation recurrence; the terminal bit must be zero, equivalent to furthest-reset parity. A zero terminal bit yields a conflict-free stable set, exhausting the possible nonempty complete extensions. Every vertex has an attacker, so the empty set is complete and grounded. Classical implications preferred⇒complete and stable⇒preferred finish the semantic classification. Counting chord sets by largest target yields the stated formulas. The package checker independently enumerates 1022 chorded-cycle frameworks of orders 4–12 and the combinatorial census through order 24; tests supplement, not replace, the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The all-chord-set last-target parity classification, complete-extension enumeration and one-third labelled perturbation census are not entailed by the inspected published statements. Zhang–Liu (2026) gives generic sufficient semantic-agreement conditions and a stable-existence equivalence involving an admissible odd-cycle hitting set, not an explicit classification of these strongly connected examples with directed odd cycles; Elaroussi (2025) gives degree-bounded algorithms and no-even-cycle uniqueness, which do not determine the chord-hub cases containing both even and odd directed cycles. value.rationale: The natural question is which localized extra attacks repair the familiar stable-semantic obstruction of an odd directed cycle, and whether the repair is unique. The theorem answers simultaneously for every subset of optional chords from one source: all nonempty complete extensions are stable, their existence depends on one last-chord parity, and the exact fraction of successful labeled repairs approaches 1/3. This is a complete structural classification over exponentially many frameworks; it is more informative than the known unchorded parity exercise and the broad sufficient path criteria. Its limitation to one chord source is explicit, and no unsupported downstream theorem is claimed.
